text:
Temporal relevance has stronger support than a fixed recent-history cutoff, but elapsed time and event distance represent different signals. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) jointly models positions and interaction intervals; its temporal mechanism is useful inspiration without adopting its causal backbone. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional attention with contrastive learning across temporally nearby interactions. [T-RoPE (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30576) further distinguishes event order, elapsed time and calendar phase through learned temporal coefficients and multiscale frequencies. These findings motivate temporal features, but do not establish improvements under the pinned Amazon evaluation.

A concrete BERT4Rec hypothesis: add jointly trained, per-head attention biases for relative event distance and bucketed log elapsed time, with content-dependent gates controlling temporal influence. This is a proposed adaptation, not a directly validated result. Compare position-only, elapsed-time-only and combined biases against fixed recent-cutoff sampling; avoid forcing every head into monotonic decay, which assumes recent purchases imply continuing demand. A [2026 BERT4Rec session study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z) explores content relevance, temporal decay and gated interest representations, offering architectural motivation rather than transferable benchmark evidence. Preserve one masked bidirectional model/checkpoint per category and appended-mask inference. Derive temporal inputs from observed training histories; use the last observed timestamp as the inference reference or a learned unknown-time representation, never the held-out target timestamp. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10.
